name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Sequential pathway of protein secretion through endomembrane

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events in the correct sequential order representing the synthesis, processing, and intracellular trafficking of a secretory protein in a eukaryotic cell:

  1. Fusion of transport vesicles with the convex cis face of the Golgi apparatus
  2. Synthesis of the protein by ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum
  3. Release of processed proteins in vesicles from the concave trans face of the Golgi apparatus
  4. Modification of proteins within the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus
  5. Packaging of synthesised proteins into transport vesicles budding from the endoplasmic reticulum

Choose the correct sequence from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the site of initial synthesis
Proteins destined for secretion or membrane targeting are translated by ribosomes attached to the outer surface of the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) and enter the ER lumen.

Step 2: Trace transition from the endoplasmic reticulum
Synthesised proteins are packaged into transport vesicles that bud off from the endoplasmic reticulum for transit to the Golgi apparatus.

Step 3: Track entry into the Golgi complex
These ER-derived vesicles migrate and fuse with the convex cis (forming) face of the Golgi apparatus, delivering their contents into the organelle's lumen.

Step 4: Trace transit through cisternae for chemical modification
Proteins move through the stacked cisternae from the forming face towards the maturing face, where post-translational modifications (such as glycosylation into glycoproteins) occur.

Step 5: Identify the terminal exit from the Golgi apparatus
Modified and sorted proteins are packaged into secretory vesicles and bud off from the concave trans (maturing) face of the Golgi apparatus to be delivered to intracellular targets or secreted across the plasma membrane.

Step 6: Final conceptual answer
The correct functional sequence is: Synthesis of the protein on the rough endoplasmic reticulum → Packaging into transport vesicles budding from the ER → Fusion of vesicles with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus → Modification of proteins within the Golgi cisternae → Release of vesicles from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus (II → V → I → IV → III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Chronological order of foundational discoveries in cell biology

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following historical milestones and discoveries in cell biology in the correct chronological order:

  1. Discovery and description of the cell nucleus by Robert Brown
  2. Proposal of the Fluid Mosaic Model of the plasma membrane by Singer and Nicolson
  3. First observation and description of a live cell by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
  4. Explanation that cells divide and new cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula) by Rudolf Virchow
  5. First observation of densely stained reticular structures (Golgi bodies) near the nucleus by Camillo Golgi

Choose the correct chronological sequence from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the earliest microscopic observation of a living cell
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first to see and describe a live cell using his improved simple microscope lenses during the late seventeenth century.

Step 2: Identify the discovery of the nucleus
Robert Brown discovered and described the nucleus as a distinct, constant organelle of the cell in 1831.

Step 3: Identify the formulation of cell origin
Rudolf Virchow in 1855 expanded and finalized the cell theory by demonstrating that cells divide and all new cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).

Step 4: Identify the observation of the Golgi apparatus
Camillo Golgi in 1898 first identified and described the densely stained reticular network near the nucleus of nerve cells, later named Golgi bodies.

Step 5: Identify the modern membrane model
Singer and Nicolson proposed the widely accepted Fluid Mosaic Model of the cell membrane in 1972, explaining the bilayer structure and lateral fluidity of proteins.

Step 6: Final conceptual answer
The correct chronological order of discoveries is: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observing a live cell → Robert Brown discovering the nucleus (1831) → Rudolf Virchow formulating Omnis cellula-e cellula (1855) → Camillo Golgi observing Golgi bodies (1898) → Singer and Nicolson proposing the fluid mosaic model (1972) (III → I → IV → V → II).
